note: Original description, with both soldier and worker; the original placed this species under Constrictotermes (Tenuirostritermes). Text taken from the OCR of a library scan on Internet Archive.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: (the original placed it in the subgenus Tenuirostritermes of the genus Constrictotermes) Head dark chestnut brown to almost black, the brown lighter around the antennal bases and at the tip of the nasus, the ventral surface of the head also paler. Head deeply constricted, the constriction angle sharp; basal half (excluding the nasus) about 1.5 times the length of the apical half, longer than the nasus and broader than the apical half; posterior part of the head rounded, with 1 long seta on each side at the widest point of the dorsal basal half. Nasus concolorous with the head, slender and elongate, acute and pale at the tip, covered with short hairs. Head forming an angle with the thorax. Antennae yellowish brown, 13 segments, covered with long hairs: segment 1 long, thick, cylindrical; segment 2 short, about half of segment 1, clavate; segment 3 long and tapering, slender at the base, almost as long as segment 1; segment 4 about equal to segment 2; segment 5 longer than segment 4 and shorter than segment 3; terminal segment long, slender, nearly oval. Pronotum yellowish brown, saddle-shaped, broader than long, the anterior margin with short hairs, the posterior margin concave. Mesonotum, metanotum and dorsal abdomen yellowish brown; abdomen covered with long golden yellow hairs, the ventral surface pale. Legs yellowish brown, long and slender. Measurements: soldier total length 2.75—3 mm; head length including nasus 1.20—1.45 mm; head length (to the anterior margin of the head, excluding nasus) 0.90—1.00 mm; nasus length 0.405—0.50 mm; combined length of abdomen and thorax 1.75—2.00 mm; pronotum length 0.105 mm; hind tibia length 0.90—0.906 mm; greatest head width 0.50—0.505 mm; pronotum width 0.307 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head chestnut brown, paler at the antennal bases, widest anteriorly, longer than broad, narrowing and becoming rounded posteriorly, covered with short hairs. Postclypeus yellowish brown, about twice as broad as long, projecting (inflated). Labrum pale yellow, widest in the middle, rounded at the apex, narrowing posteriorly, hairy anteriorly. Antennae yellow, longer than the head, 13—14 segments, covered with long hairs: segment 1 long, thick, cylindrical; segment 2 clavate, short, about half of segment 1; segment 3 longer than segment 2, clavate, slender at the base, shorter than segment 1; segment 4 clavate, short, about as long as segment 2; segment 5 clavate, rather long; terminal segment long, slender, nearly oval. Pronotum paler than the head, saddle-shaped, broader than long, the anterior and lateral margins covered with short hairs. Mesonotum, metanotum and dorsal abdomen of the same colour as the pronotum; the ventral surface paler, covered with long golden yellow hairs. Legs yellow, long, hairy. Measurements: worker total length 3.60—4.00 mm; combined length of abdomen and thorax 2.75—3.00 mm; head length 1.40—1.50 mm; hind tibia length 1.10 mm; head width 1.10 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type locality San Pedro, Honduras (inland, the terminus of the railway running from Puerto Cortes), collected by W. M. Mann. Snyder described the worker from a series of workers from the same lot as the typical soldier. He discussed that this species, like C. briciae, is known from only one soldier morph, has very few head hairs and very short mandibles, that the soldier legs are as long as in the various species of Tenuirostritermes, and that the worker postclypeus is about twice as broad as long, and therefore placed it in the subgenus Tenuirostritermes.
